structure.title: Act I · A promise without instructions
structure.text: The witches predict a crown. They never tell Macbeth to kill the king. In the interval between hearing the prediction and receiving Duncan as a guest, Macbeth and his wife supply a great deal of the missing plot themselves.

structure.title: Acts II–III · A crown without sleep
structure.text: The murder that seemed to promise an end to suspense makes every ordinary sound unbearable. Macbeth discovers he can give orders privately, even from his wife. The public test of the new household comes at a dinner party.

structure.title: Acts IV–V · The country outside the castle
structure.text: Macbeth seeks fresh assurances. Elsewhere a household, refugees and soldiers reveal what his search for security costs people who never heard a prophecy. Scotland becomes visible as a place that has to survive its king.

people.name: Lady Macbeth
people.text: She knows which doubts her husband will voice and how to make him ashamed of them. Her practical attention to clothes, faces and doors makes the undertaking possible. Keeping a face composed grows harder than cleaning a room.

people.name: Banquo
people.role: The other hearer of the prophecy
people.text: He hears promises about his descendants. Having a second soldier present matters because it lets the play show two men hearing the same voices and finding different obligations in what they say.

context.title: A king staying the night
context.text: Duncan enters as Macbeth's sovereign, kinsman and guest. Each relation gives his host a reason to protect him. The preparations required to violate those obligations look uncomfortably like preparations for a successful visit.

context.title: What a prophecy leaves unsaid
context.text: Macbeth receives a prediction about a title he does not yet possess. One prediction comes true almost immediately through somebody else’s decision. It gives him a reason to trust the next one, while leaving entirely open what, if anything, he must do about it.

passages.quote: All hail, Macbeth! that shalt be king hereafter!

notice.text: Listen to who uses the word man.
notice.why: Courage earned Macbeth praise in battle. At home the same ideal can be used to shame him into killing a sleeping guest. Later another husband finds words for manhood that leave room for grief.

notice.text: Keep hearing the knocking after the murder.
notice.why: Somebody outside simply expects a door to open. Getting the household back onto ordinary time becomes an alarming amount of work.

opening: Macbeth is a successful soldier when three strangers tell him he will be king. He could wait to see whether they are right. Instead, he begins imagining what would have to happen to make them right, and his wife recognises an opportunity he is frightened to name. Shakespeare follows an ambition from its first private permission into the practical work of keeping power. The terrible intimacy is that Macbeth can see what he is becoming while he is still choosing it.
